messages:
maya: Heads up — since ~02:10 UTC we're seeing grpc deadline_exceeded spikes and intermittent streaming token stalls for eu-west GPUs. Affected pods are mostly on the gpu-pool-a autoscaler group.
jonathan: saw that too. metrics show p99 latency for /v1/stream jump and a pattern of TCP retransmits + reorder counters on a few hosts.
ryan: any kernel or NIC change last night?
lina: Yes, we rolled kernel 6.1->6.2 on the node image at 01:30 UTC for that pool. No infra-level MTU change planned.
maya: logs show lots of "stream stalled, seq=###" in the runtime agent and grpc logs: 
```
rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
runtime: stream stall at token_seq=4200 last_ack=4189
```
jonathan: Looking at ethtool counters on mlx5 cores: tx_reorder and rx_reorder increments on 3 hosts, plus GRO/GSO flips after kernel upgrade.
ryan: Could be offload/large segment handling regression. If GRO/GSO is inconsistent across path you get reordering at OS level which breaks our streaming assumptions (we rely on in-order TCP for token delivery).
lina: Also noticed MTU mismatch on one node: one pod's veth showed 9000 but the overlay device was 1500 after CNI reconfig. Might cause fragmentation/segmentation and reordering under load.
maya: Workaround idea: enforce MTU 1500 across the path + disable GRO temporarily on the affected nodes to see if reorder counters stop. Can we patch a small daemonset?
ryan: Agree. I can push a rolling daemonset that sets: 
```
# stop GRO/GSO
ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# ensure MTU
ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500
```
jonathan: Before we flip, let's fail-open for high-priority customers: scale up fallback_local model replicas (lower-cap priority) and enable grpc timeouts to 10s to reduce transient hits.
lina: I'll add a kube-rollout pause window and mark the node pool cordoned for scheduling while we test.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-341 (label: networking/reorder). Assigned to eng-infra.
ryan: Rolling daemonset pushed to 3 hosts in eu-west-A. Early telemetry: reorder counters stabilized and token stream resumed for those pods.
maya: Nice. But we still see a few sub-second jitter spikes on other hosts — likely RDMA (RoCEv2) flows on the same leaf switch causing microbursts.
jonathan: On RDMA we should check PFC settings and counters. If ECN thresholding triggered, it can reorder packets when congestion control kicks in. I'll pull switch counters with the fabric team.
lina: For now, leaving GRO off on all gpu-pool-a nodes and pinning MTU 1500. I'll also add a config flag in the node image to keep this persistent.
ryan: Post-mortem notes: kernel 6.2 changed default offload behavior on mlx5 -> reordering under heavy GSO/GRO + MTU mismatch + RDMA microbursts. Action items: revert node image, schedule kernel vendor backport, add e2e test that simulates token streaming under high reorder.
maya: Also add alert rule: if tcp_retransmits or net_reorder > 50/min on any gpu node, auto-disable GRO and notify SRE.
jonathan: I'll open the follow-up ticket with logs, node list, and timeline.
infra-bot: Patch deployed to gpu-pool-a: gro/gso disabled on 8 nodes, MTU enforced. Monitoring: https://redwood.metrics/alerts/INC-2025-341
maya: Thanks team — keep this thread updated if anything flares back up. :thumbsup:
